tips.text: Eswatini’s landscape is known for its **green, wooded hills** and **tall golden grass**.
tips.note: In contrast, Lesotho’s mountains are typically barren, and long grass is not a common sight there.

tips.text: Poles in Eswatini are made of **dark brown wood** and follow a simple design. The insulators are mostly mounted on the side.
tips.note: In Southern Africa, three insulators on the pole are more commonly found in Eswatini.

tips.text: Roads starting with the letters **“MR”** are exclusive to Eswatini.
Eswatini typically uses **yellow **outside lines and occasionally, **triple white **middle lines.
tips.note: Similar road lines can also be found in South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana.

tips.text: All of Eswatini was covered by a **white** Google car without an antenna.
tips.note: Within Africa, this car can also be found in South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana.

tips.text: **Concrete bus shelters** are a common sight on roads in Eswatini.
Montane grasslands with **long golden grass** and a mountainous landscape are typical of Western Eswatini.
tips.note: Long grass can be found in almost all areas of Eswatini. This clue refers specifically to the pristine golden colour most commonly seen in the Western highlands.

tips.text: **Pine tree plantations** are found in select areas in the West of the country.
tips.note: Similar plantations can also be found in South Africa.

tips.text: This distinct region in the central South of the country, mostly along the MR9, can be recognized by the dark, overwhelming **greenness** and **tall wooded mountains**.
tips.note: If you are struggling to see why this is unique, try comparing this to other areas of the country, which are more “golden” and light-coloured.

tips.text: You can recognise this region in the east of the country thanks to the **unusual flatness** and the mountains often visible in the distance.
**Sugar cane **is grown in several areas along the Eastern border.
The MR3 South of Ngomane can be recognized thanks to flatness, long dry grass and the **dirt on the camera**.
The MR3 from Manzini to the South African border is **divided** by metal and stone guardrails, making it recognisable.
tips.note: This road is the only divided highway found in Eswatini.

tips.text: The MR8 in Southeastern Eswatini straddling the South African border is recognisable because of this **distinct ridge to the east**.
You can recognise the **Mlawula Nature Reserve** thanks to the narrow dirt tracks, tall grass and overall savannah landscape.
If you see **Portuguese** text in Eswatini, you are most likely in the small town of Lomahasha.
tips.note: This is because of its proximity to Mozambique, where Portuguese is spoken.
